content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 1-2. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 terminology. This unit focuses on architecture description and architecture reality.

An architecture description is a communicative artifact. It may include views, diagrams, principles, models, decisions, scenarios, constraints, and explanations. The real architecture is the system and its consequential design choices; the description is the recorded representation used for communication and analysis.

This distinction matters because documentation can become either too vague to guide work or too exhaustive to maintain. Good architecture description records the structures and decisions that stakeholders need for design, review, implementation, testing, deployment, and evolution.
Studio: compare a code repository README, a deployment diagram, and a decision record. Decide which parts describe the architecture and which parts merely describe project logistics.

concepts.name: Architecture description
concepts.description: A set of artifacts that records an architecture so stakeholders can understand, analyze, and use it.

concepts.name: Architecture view
concepts.description: A representation of a system from the perspective of one set of concerns.

concepts.name: Architecture model
concepts.description: A structured representation of architectural elements and relationships used for reasoning or communication.

concepts.name: Documentation fitness
concepts.description: The degree to which architecture documentation is useful, current, concise, and aligned with stakeholder needs.
